Which latency instrument reports the true p95 and what does it miss

label: The health folder is mostly synthetic: 15,400 of 17,775 duration rows (86.6 percent) sit in 77 generated sweeps of 200 monotone 101-300 ms values, leaving 2,375 real rows across 381 files.
Real built-state hook cost is p50 12, p95 279, p99 735, max 2,218 ms over all real rows; live-only it is p50 124, p95 311, p99 757, max 1,538 ms.
The 300 ms cliff reported in iteration 1 was the sweep's ceiling: 4,674 plateau rows are the top 60 rows of each 77-file sweep, and the real rows show a smooth tail to 1,538 ms.
The 2,218 ms maximum is an unavailable row, not a delivered brief; 664 unavailable rows have p50 0 ms and p95 2 ms, and every live row is at or below 1,538 ms.
The instrument cannot show a cold-start cost: an unavailable prompt stores 0 ms rather than its probe time, so the population where a cold start would appear reports no elapsed time.

Coverage is Claude-dominated: 1,794 of 2,375 real rows (75.5 percent) are claude, against pi 272, dsh 131, devin 117, vibe 49, codex 12 and cursor 0; per-runtime live p95s are claude 292, dsh 243, devin 230, pi 179, vibe 742 ms.
Live p95 311 ms is 12.4 percent of the 2,500 ms hook budget, live p99 757 ms is 30.3 percent, and the worst live row 1,538 ms is 61.5 percent; no live row of 1,695 exceeded the budget.
Brief cost on real rows is unchanged: 1,234 briefs, mean 270.6 bytes, p50 262, p95 316, max 361.

The product's rolling rate reads only a workspace's last 30 records, so real workspaces are unaffected, but any cross-workspace aggregate reports the synthetic shape unless it filters by file or runtime.
